diagnosis: Gastric Kaposi sarcoma in a patient with HIV
legend: A The typical features of Kaposi sarcoma can be masked by inflammation. In this case, a mucosal prominence containing mostly inflammation and what appeared to be granulation tissue showed a subtle spindle cell proliferation along the blood vessels.
B The HHV8 stain is positive in a subtle case of Kaposi sarcoma masked by inflammation and resembling granulation tissue.

KSHV/HHV8 positivity in a rectal mass from a patient with AIDS. This is KSHV/HHV8 stain from the rectal Kaposi sarcoma case that resembled granulation tissue. The small, spindled cells show nuclear positivity.

Lymphangioma-like rectal Kaposi sarcoma in a patient with AIDS. Multiple morphological appearances can occur in the same tumour. This lymphangioma-like morphology of Kaposi sarcoma occurred in the same sample as the case resembling granulation tissue. In this part of the tumour, the lesional cells are small, dilated vessels, which were positive for KSHV/HHV8.

Lymphangioma-like rectal Kaposi sarcoma, positive for KSHV/HHV8 immunohistochemical stain. The small lymphatic channels are positive for KSHV/HHV8. This part of the tumour did not show spindle cells, but the haemosiderin deposits and the history of a rectal mass in the context of AIDS raised the possibility of Kaposi sarcoma, confirmed by this immunostain.
